summary: Dennis Hirota specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his B.A. and M.A. at UC Berkeley and his Ph.D. at Nagoya University. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University around 1996 and was affiliated with Hongwanji International Center in 1998.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Derek F. Maher earned his B.A. from Evergreen State College and his M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, later co-directing religious studies at East Carolina University.

Dermot Killingley is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Oxford and SOAS University of London. He held positions at the University of Malaya, served as a Senior Lecturer at Newcastle University, and became Reader in Religious Studies there.

A specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Dermott Joseph Walsh received his BA from Trinity College Dublin, an MA from Leiden University, and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2018 under William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramkrishna Bhandarkar worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta around 1910 and as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India from 1911 to 1917.

Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen, with Leo K. Shin serving as a committee member.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima studied under Gaton Ngawang Legpa, Ngawang Nyima, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche. From 1960 to 1972, he participated in a research project at the University of Washington.

Dhammanandā is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, also studying under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama.

Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and studied under traditional teacher Dhammasakkaro. He was attested as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong in 2013.
Dhirendra Mohan Datta worked in philosophy and Indology after studying at the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Patna College in 1928 and at the University of Minnesota from 1951 to 1952.
Dhirendra Sharma was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and the traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Dhivan Thomas Jones studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held posts as an associate lecturer at the Open University and at the University of Chester in 2019.

Di Luo specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Luo earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Southern California under doctoral supervisors Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, having completed an MA supervised by James Steele.
Diana L. Eck specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Smith College, SOAS University of London, and Harvard University, where she later became a professor around 1976.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She served as an Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art, attested in 2005.

Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford. Her posts include Visiting Assistant Professor positions at Pepperdine University and Kenyon College, and Faculty Specialist at Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who was a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen.
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at École Polytechnique under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA at Peking University and completed his PhD in 2019 at the University of California, Los Angeles.
